headline: This law puts the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center into the Homeland Security Act and sets out its duties, who it trains, and how it can spend and charge money.
what_it_does: The law writes the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC) into the Homeland Security Act of 2002 as part of the Department of Homeland Security, led by a director who reports to the DHS Secretary. It lists the center's job duties, including building training programs, managing facilities, sharing homeland security information, and helping train foreign police. It lets FLETC train federal employees, state and local police, and private sector groups, and it sets rules for partner agencies, fees, housing, and travel costs. It also makes existing spending and gift authorities permanent, including money to honor graduates who died in the line of duty.

who_it_affects.group: Federal law enforcement and homeland security employees
who_it_affects.how: They may be trained at FLETC facilities, off-site, or online, and some are expected to live in FLETC housing when practical.

who_it_affects.group: State and local law enforcement agencies
who_it_affects.how: They can enter partnerships with FLETC for training, and the center may charge them fees for training.

who_it_affects.group: Partner federal agencies with a memorandum of understanding with FLETC
who_it_affects.how: They must pay for and assign detailed instructors to training programs without reimbursement.
FLETC may coordinate with them to provide training and share homeland security information.

who_it_affects.group: Retired federal employees with training experience
who_it_affects.how: FLETC may hire them to work at the center.

who_it_affects.group: Families of FLETC graduates who died in the line of duty
who_it_affects.how: FLETC may spend funds to honor and memorialize those graduates.
